title: 2nd Stopping Place 1st Truth Grandeur And Sublimity

questions.question: What is the first truth named in the target passage?
questions.answer: It is the truth of grandeur and sublimity.

questions.question: Why does the passage give only a brief treatment of this truth?
questions.answer: Because fuller proofs are said to be explained elsewhere in the same body of writings.

questions.question: What large-scale example from the universe is used to show one Being’s power over distant things?
questions.answer: The passage points to the creation and control of stars that are extremely far apart.

questions.question: What example from plant life shows one pattern being given across the whole earth at the same time?
questions.answer: It mentions countless flowers of the same kind appearing in one shared form across different regions of the world.

questions.question: About how many kinds of plants and animals are described as being managed in a short seasonal period?
questions.answer: More than two hundred thousand kinds are mentioned.

questions.question: How long is that seasonal period said to be?
questions.answer: About five or six weeks.

questions.question: What qualities mark this springtime ordering of living things?
questions.answer: It is described as regular, balanced, and free of confusion, flaw, and mistake.

questions.question: What yearly event is presented as a sign resembling a great rising to life?
questions.answer: Spring is presented as displaying many examples of a supreme resurrection on earth.

questions.question: What earlier unseen event is spring said to help prove to human beings?
questions.answer: It helps point to the creation of the heavens and the earth.

questions.question: Besides creating living beings, what ongoing movement of the earth is mentioned?
questions.answer: The earth’s turning is mentioned.

questions.question: What image is used for the relation between night and day?
questions.answer: Night is pictured like a page on which the events of the day are recorded.

questions.question: What does the same Being know and manage in human beings?
questions.answer: He knows and governs even the hidden thoughts in people’s hearts.

questions.question: How does the passage connect many different acts to one conclusion about their Doer?
questions.answer: It says these acts are really one act, so they point to one unique and powerful Doer.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does this grandeur leave no room for?
questions.answer: It leaves no room at all for accepting any partner with Allah.

questions.question: Does the passage merely reduce the possibility of partnership, or what stronger claim does it make?
questions.answer: It makes the stronger claim that such grandeur completely tears out that possibility from the root.

questions.question: Why would assigning partners suggest weakness or need?
questions.answer: Because it would mean the divine power was not sufficient by itself.

questions.question: What would assigning partners wrongly imply about divine grandeur, perfection, and all-embracing rule?
questions.answer: It would suggest fault in grandeur, defect in perfection, and limits in what is all-encompassing.

questions.question: How does the passage judge the idea that a sound mind could accept such a claim?
questions.answer: It says no sound intellect could regard it as possible.

questions.question: Why is associating partners with Allah described as such a serious sin here?
questions.answer: Because it is treated as an offense against His greatness, glory, and sublimity.

questions.question: What Qur’anic ruling is cited to show the seriousness of this sin?
questions.answer: The passage cites that associating partners is not forgiven, while lesser sins may be forgiven.

questions.question: What is the title of the second truth introduced at the end of the target passage?
questions.answer: It is the absoluteness, comprehensiveness, and endless manifestation of dominical deeds in the cosmos.

questions.question: What alone is said to set limits on those deeds?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will set their limits, along with the capacities of the things and places where they appear.

questions.question: Which false explanations are rejected as partners in these deeds?
questions.answer: Chance, nature, blind force, unconscious causation, and scattered elements are all rejected.

questions.question: If those things do not truly create, what role are they said to have?
questions.answer: They are only outward means used as a veil over divine power.

questions.question: How many examples does the passage say will be given for the second truth?
questions.answer: It says three examples will be presented from verses in Surah al-Nahl.

questions.question: What central belief does the first truth defend?
questions.answer: It defends Allah’s oneness by showing that no partner can share His rule.

questions.question: Which two qualities are joined together in the title of the first truth?
questions.answer: Grandeur and sublimity.

questions.question: What does the passage say about stars that are far apart?
questions.answer: One Being creates and directs them together at the same time and in one way.

questions.question: How does the passage use flowers to show unity in creation?
questions.answer: It says countless flowers of one species are produced in the same pattern across the earth.

questions.question: What wide geographic spread is mentioned for these flowers?
questions.answer: They are spread through east and west and north and south.

questions.question: What kinds of living things are especially emphasized in spring?
questions.answer: Many types of plants and animals are emphasized.

questions.question: What does the passage stress about the way these creatures are handled?
questions.answer: They are sustained, brought to life, distinguished, and decorated with perfect order.

questions.question: What signs show that this work is not random?
questions.answer: There is balance, regularity, and no confusion or error.

questions.question: Why is spring compared to resurrection?
questions.answer: Because many forms of life return in a striking and repeated way before human eyes.

questions.question: What connection is made between spring and the six-day creation of the heavens and the earth?
questions.answer: Spring is presented as a visible sign helping people accept that earlier act of creation.

questions.question: What daily cosmic process is mentioned after the spring examples?
questions.answer: The passing of night into day and day into night.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by saying day’s events are written onto night?
questions.answer: It suggests an orderly, controlled unfolding of time under divine management.

questions.question: How far does divine knowledge reach according to this passage?
questions.answer: It reaches even the most hidden thoughts in human hearts.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from all these many acts being treated as one act?
questions.answer: Their Maker and Manager must be one unique and all-powerful Being.

questions.question: What effect does divine grandeur have on the idea of shirk?
questions.answer: It blocks it completely and leaves no opening for it.

questions.question: What would shirk wrongly imply about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It would imply that His power has weakness or need.

questions.question: What would shirk wrongly imply about Allah’s perfection?
questions.answer: It would imply that perfection is missing something.

questions.question: What would shirk wrongly imply about Allah’s all-encompassing rule?
questions.answer: It would imply that His reach is limited.

questions.question: How does the passage appeal to reason in rejecting shirk?
questions.answer: It says a sound and healthy mind would never accept such a claim.

questions.question: Why is shirk described here as more than just an intellectual mistake?
questions.answer: Because it is also presented as a grave offense against divine majesty and glory.

questions.question: What divine response from the Qur’an is mentioned regarding this offense?
questions.answer: The Qur’an warns that associating partners with Allah is not forgiven, though lesser sins may be.

questions.question: What three features describe the second truth’s view of divine deeds?
questions.answer: They are absolute, all-encompassing, and appearing without limit.

questions.question: What two things are said to determine how those deeds appear in creation?
questions.answer: Divine wisdom and will, along with the capacities of created things and places.

questions.question: Why are chance and blind causes ruled out?
questions.answer: Because the deeds of creation are balanced, wise, life-giving, orderly, and firm.

questions.question: If natural causes are not true makers, how are they portrayed?
questions.answer: They are portrayed as outward coverings that hide the direct operation of divine power.

questions.question: What is the main topic of the target passage’s first section?
questions.answer: It explains how Allah’s greatness and exaltedness point to His oneness.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention other writings before giving examples?
questions.answer: To say that this section is only a shortened presentation, not the full discussion.

questions.question: What is significant about creating stars that are separated by huge distances at the same time?
questions.answer: It shows one power reaching everywhere without difficulty or division.

questions.question: What does producing the same kind of flower across the globe suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests one will and one design working over all regions.

questions.question: Why is the number of plant and animal types important in the argument?
questions.answer: It highlights the massive variety being handled together without disorder.

questions.question: What does the short time of five or six weeks emphasize?
questions.answer: It emphasizes speed and ease in managing vast numbers of living things.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention nurturing, reviving, distinguishing, and adorning creatures?
questions.answer: To show that creation includes many connected actions, all carried out in perfect harmony.

questions.question: What does the phrase about no confusion, defect, or error help prove?
questions.answer: It helps prove that the work comes from perfect wisdom, not scattered causes.

questions.question: How is spring used as evidence for belief in the unseen?
questions.answer: It gives a visible repeated sign that supports belief in a past divine act of creation.

questions.question: What does the rotation of the earth add to the overall argument?
questions.answer: It adds another example of large-scale order controlled by the same divine power.

questions.question: How does the passage move from cosmic signs to human inner life?
questions.answer: It says the same Being also knows and directs the secret thoughts in hearts.

questions.question: What does that shift from stars to hearts show?
questions.answer: It shows divine knowledge and power cover both the vast and the hidden.

questions.question: Why does the passage say these many deeds are really one deed?
questions.answer: Because they are all expressions of one unified divine action, not separate competing powers.

questions.question: What kind of Being is inferred from that unity of action?
questions.answer: A single, unique, and mighty Being.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does true grandeur do to the idea of having partners?
questions.answer: It makes that idea impossible.

questions.question: What four wrong ideas would partnership force someone to accept about Allah?
questions.answer: Weakness, need, imperfection, and limitation.

questions.question: Why is limitation especially important in this argument?
questions.answer: Because the passage insists divine greatness includes everything and cannot be confined.

questions.question: What role does human reason play in this section?
questions.answer: Reason is called to recognize that partnership with Allah is impossible.

questions.question: How is shirk evaluated morally as well as intellectually?
questions.answer: It is presented both as false and as a serious crime against divine majesty.

questions.question: What Qur’anic teaching is used to underline the gravity of shirk?
questions.answer: The teaching that Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, though He forgives lesser sins.

questions.question: What broad subject does the second truth introduce?
questions.answer: It introduces the all-embracing and unrestricted nature of divine lordly actions in the universe.

questions.question: What does the passage say keeps these deeds from appearing in a random or uncontrolled way?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will, together with the capacities of created things.

questions.question: Why are nature and force called inadequate explanations?
questions.answer: Because they are blind and unconscious, while the deeds described are wise and precise.

questions.question: How are material causes treated in relation to divine power?
questions.answer: They are treated as coverings or veils, not real independent agents.

questions.question: What does the promise of three examples suggest about the next stage of the argument?
questions.answer: It suggests that the author will support the claim with concrete cases from revelation and creation.

questions.question: What name is given to the first truth in the marked passage?
questions.answer: It is called the truth of grandeur and sublimity.

questions.question: Is the discussion presented as complete or selective?
questions.answer: It is selective and limited to a few points.

questions.question: What is one sign of divine control in the heavens mentioned here?
questions.answer: The stars, though very far from each other, are created and governed together.

questions.question: What earthly example parallels that heavenly example?
questions.answer: Flowers of the same species are brought forth across the whole world in one common pattern.

questions.question: What season is especially highlighted as a display of divine action?
questions.answer: Spring.

questions.question: During spring, what two major groups of living things are mentioned?
questions.answer: Plants and animals.

questions.question: What number is given to show the huge variety in spring?
questions.answer: More than two hundred thousand types are mentioned.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the quality of this seasonal work?
questions.answer: It is done with precision, balance, and without mistakes.

questions.question: How does spring serve as a lesson for people?
questions.answer: It places before them many visible examples of life returning after death-like stillness.

questions.question: What unseen event is supported by that yearly lesson?
questions.answer: The original creation of the heavens and the earth.

questions.question: What regular motion connected to time is brought into the discussion?
questions.answer: The turning that brings night and day into each other.

questions.question: What metaphor is used to describe night?
questions.answer: It is compared to a page that receives the record of daily events.

questions.question: How personal is divine knowledge according to this passage?
questions.answer: It extends to the deepest and most hidden thoughts in people’s hearts.

questions.question: What does the passage conclude about the Doer behind all these actions?
questions.answer: The Doer must be one and uniquely powerful.

questions.question: Why can no partner be accepted alongside that Doer?
questions.answer: Because His greatness and exaltedness allow no room for any shared control.

questions.question: What insult to divine power would partnership involve?
questions.answer: It would treat that power as if it needed help or lacked full strength.

questions.question: What insult to divine perfection would partnership involve?
questions.answer: It would suggest imperfection or deficiency.

questions.question: What insult to divine comprehensiveness would partnership involve?
questions.answer: It would act as though His rule does not include everything.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the judgment of a sound intellect on this issue?
questions.answer: A sound intellect would reject such partnership as impossible.

questions.question: Why is shirk described as a very serious crime in this section?
questions.answer: Because it offends Allah’s grandeur, glory, and sublimity.

questions.question: What Qur’anic message is brought as a warning?
questions.answer: That associating partners with Allah is not pardoned, while lesser sins may be pardoned.

questions.question: What is the second truth mainly about?
questions.answer: It is about the unrestricted and all-encompassing divine acts seen throughout the cosmos.

questions.question: What controls and directs those acts?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will direct them.

questions.question: What also affects how those acts appear in the world?
questions.answer: The built-in capacities of the things and places where they show up.

questions.question: What view does the passage take of chance, nature, force, and causality?
questions.answer: It denies that they have any real share in the Creator’s wise and orderly deeds.

questions.question: If those things are not true causes, what are they like instead?
questions.answer: They are like outward screens behind which divine power works.

questions.question: How many examples does the passage announce before the target section ends?
questions.answer: It announces three examples.

questions.question: What truth is presented first in the target passage?
questions.answer: The first truth is the truth of grandeur and sublimity.

questions.question: How does the passage describe its own treatment of that truth?
questions.answer: It says the treatment here is brief because fuller proofs exist elsewhere.

questions.question: What does creating and governing distant stars together show about the Creator?
questions.answer: It shows unlimited reach and unified control.

questions.question: What does producing the same flower species across the earth show?
questions.answer: It shows one command and one pattern working everywhere.

questions.question: Why is the mention of every direction of the globe important?
questions.answer: It shows that divine action is not local or partial but worldwide.

questions.question: What huge number of living kinds appears in the spring example?
questions.answer: More than two hundred thousand types of plants and animals.

questions.question: What actions are performed for those creatures in spring?
questions.answer: They are governed, fed, revived, distinguished, and beautified.

questions.question: What result would we expect if multiple independent powers were involved, and what does the passage say instead?
questions.answer: We would expect disorder, but the passage says there is regularity and balance without error.

questions.question: In what way is spring a sign of revival after death?
questions.answer: It brings vast numbers of living forms back again each year.

questions.question: What past divine act is this repeated springtime sign meant to support?
questions.answer: It supports belief in the creation of the heavens and the earth.

questions.question: What example from daily life in the universe is added after spring?
questions.answer: The alternation and interweaving of night and day.

questions.question: Why is the mention of hidden thoughts important to the argument?
questions.answer: It shows the same divine rule covers the inner world of humans as well as the outer cosmos.

questions.question: What logical conclusion does the passage draw from all these acts being one in reality?
questions.answer: That their agent is one unique and mighty Being.

questions.question: What phrase best summarizes the passage’s judgment on divine partnership?
questions.answer: It is entirely impossible.

questions.question: Why would accepting partners amount to claiming divine weakness?
questions.answer: Because help or sharing would mean the power is not absolute.

questions.question: Why would accepting partners amount to claiming divine need?
questions.answer: Because a partner would be treated like something necessary.

questions.question: Why would accepting partners amount to claiming defect?
questions.answer: Because it would deny the fullness of divine perfection.

questions.question: Why would accepting partners amount to claiming restriction?
questions.answer: Because it would deny that divine greatness embraces all things.

questions.question: What standard of thinking is called on to reject this idea?
questions.answer: Sound intellect.

questions.question: How does the passage connect theology and sin in its discussion of shirk?
questions.answer: It presents shirk as both false belief and a grave moral offense.

questions.question: What punishment-related teaching from the Qur’an is used as evidence?
questions.answer: The teaching that shirk is not forgiven, though lesser wrongs may be forgiven.

questions.question: What is emphasized about dominical deeds in the second truth?
questions.answer: Their absolute, comprehensive, and limitless appearance throughout the universe.

questions.question: According to the passage, what limits those deeds in their manifestations?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will, plus the capacities of created things and places.

questions.question: What qualities of divine deeds make blind causes impossible explanations?
questions.answer: Their wisdom, balance, order, life-giving character, and firmness.

questions.question: How does the passage reinterpret apparent causes?
questions.answer: It treats them as veils used by divine command, will, and power.

questions.question: What source is named for the three upcoming examples?
questions.answer: Three connected verses in Surah al-Nahl.

questions.question: What heading introduces the first major section of the target passage?
questions.answer: The truth of grandeur and sublimity.

questions.question: What does the passage say about where more detailed proofs can be found?
questions.answer: It says they are found in other parts of the same collection of writings.

questions.question: What astronomical example is used to show unified creation and administration?
questions.answer: The stars, even though separated by vast distances, are managed together by one Being.

questions.question: What botanical example is used to show a common pattern across the world?
questions.answer: Countless flowers of one species are created in one form across the earth.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens every spring on earth?
questions.answer: Huge numbers of living forms appear again in an orderly and balanced way.

questions.question: How many kinds of plants and animals are mentioned in that spring scene?
questions.answer: More than two hundred thousand.

questions.question: What time frame increases the force of that example?
questions.answer: It all happens within about five or six weeks.

questions.question: Which words in the passage show precision in this process?
questions.answer: It emphasizes regularity, equilibrium, and the absence of confusion, flaw, and error.

questions.question: Why is spring called a display of resurrection-like signs?
questions.answer: Because it shows many examples of life being brought forth again.

questions.question: What foundational act of creation is linked to that yearly sign?
questions.answer: The creation of the heavens and the earth.

questions.question: What ongoing process involving time and the earth is cited next?
questions.answer: The mingling and succession of night and day through the earth’s movement.

questions.question: How does the passage describe divine awareness of the human inner world?
questions.answer: It says even the most hidden thoughts of hearts are known and governed.

questions.question: What argument is built from combining control of stars, spring, day and night, and hearts?
questions.answer: That one and the same Being carries out all these acts.

questions.question: What quality of that Being makes partnership impossible?
questions.answer: His majestic greatness and exalted power.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does this greatness do to the idea of partnership?
questions.answer: It leaves not even the smallest opening for it.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying greatness is at the peak of perfection?
questions.answer: It means divine majesty is complete and lacks nothing.

questions.question: Why would a partner imply fault in divine glory?
questions.answer: Because sharing rule would suggest that glory is not fully complete in itself.

questions.question: Why would a partner imply a boundary on divine comprehensiveness?
questions.answer: Because it would assign part of reality outside His sole command.

questions.question: How does the passage evaluate such a belief from the viewpoint of reason?
questions.answer: It says reasonable and healthy-minded people cannot accept it.

questions.question: Why is shirk described as especially serious before Allah?
questions.answer: Because it violates His grandeur, the honor of His glory, and His sublimity.

questions.question: What Qur’anic principle is cited to show how grave shirk is?
questions.answer: That Allah does not forgive association of partners, while He may forgive lesser sins.

questions.question: What is the name of the second truth introduced afterward?
questions.answer: The absoluteness, comprehensiveness, and infinite manifestation of dominical deeds in the cosmos.

questions.question: What two factors are said to determine the limits of those deeds as they appear?
questions.answer: Divine wisdom and will, and the capacities of creatures and places.

questions.question: Which supposed causes are dismissed as unable to share in these deeds?
questions.answer: Random chance, nature, blind force, unconscious causation, and the scattered elements.

questions.question: What features of the deeds prove those supposed causes inadequate?
questions.answer: The deeds are balanced, wise, insightful, life-giving, orderly, and firm.

questions.question: What role is left for those apparent causes?
questions.answer: They serve only as outward veils hiding the direct action of divine power.

questions.question: How many illustrative examples does the passage promise next?
questions.answer: Three examples.
